entries.originalText: O Lord God, I see that patience is very necessary unto me; for many things in this life fall out contrary.
entries.modernizedText: O Lord God, I see that patience is very necessary to me; for many things in this life turn out contrary to my wishes.

entries.originalText: For howsoever I may have contrived for my peace, my life cannot go on without strife and trouble.
entries.modernizedText: For however I may have planned for my peace, my life cannot go on without strife and trouble.

entries.originalText: “Thou speakest truly, My Son.
entries.modernizedText: “You speak truly, My Son.

entries.originalText: For I will not that thou seek such a peace as is without trials, and knoweth no adversities; but rather that thou shouldest judge thyself to have found peace, when thou art tried with manifold tribulations, and proved by many adversities.
entries.modernizedText: For I do not will that you seek a peace that is without trials and knows no adversities; but rather that you should judge yourself to have found peace when you are tried with manifold tribulations and tested by many adversities.

entries.originalText: If thou shalt say that thou art not able to bear much, how then wilt thou sustain the fire hereafter?
entries.modernizedText: If you say that you are not able to bear much, how then will you sustain the fire hereafter?

entries.originalText: Of two evils we should always choose the less.
entries.modernizedText: Of two evils we should always choose the lesser.

entries.originalText: Therefore, that thou mayest escape eternal torments hereafter, strive on God’s behalf to endure present evils bravely.
entries.modernizedText: Therefore, that you may escape eternal torments hereafter, strive on God’s behalf to endure present evils bravely.

entries.originalText: Thinkest thou that the children of this world suffer nought, or but little?
entries.modernizedText: Do you think that the children of this world suffer nothing, or but little?

entries.originalText: Thou wilt not find it so, even though thou find out the most prosperous.
entries.modernizedText: You will not find it so, even if you find the most prosperous.

entries.originalText: “‘But,’ thou wilt say, ‘they have many delights, and they follow their own wills, and thus they bear lightly their tribulations.’
entries.modernizedText: “‘But,’ you will say, ‘they have many delights, and they follow their own wills, and thus they bear their tribulations lightly.’

entries.originalText: “Be it so, grant that they have what they list; but how long, thinkest thou, will it last?
entries.modernizedText: “Be it so, grant that they have what they wish; but how long, do you think, will it last?

entries.originalText: Behold, like the smoke those who are rich in this world will pass away, and no record shall remain of their past joys.
entries.modernizedText: Behold, like smoke those who are rich in this world will pass away, and no record will remain of their past joys.

entries.originalText: Yea, even while they yet live, they rest not without bitterness and weariness and fear.
entries.modernizedText: Indeed, even while they yet live, they do not rest without bitterness and weariness and fear.

entries.originalText: For from the very same thing wherein they find delight, thence they oftentimes have the punishment of sorrow.
entries.modernizedText: For from the very same thing in which they find delight, they often have the punishment of sorrow.

entries.originalText: Justly it befalleth them, that because out of measure they seek out and pursue pleasures, they enjoy them not without confusion and bitterness.
entries.modernizedText: Justly it happens to them that, because they seek out and pursue pleasures beyond measure, they do not enjoy them without confusion and bitterness.

entries.originalText: Oh how short, how false, how inordinate and wicked are all these pleasures!
entries.modernizedText: Oh how short, how false, how inordinate and wicked are all these pleasures!

entries.originalText: Yet because of their sottishness and blindness men do not understand; but like brute beasts, for the sake of a little pleasure of this corruptible life, they incur death of the soul.
entries.modernizedText: Yet because of their foolishness and blindness men do not understand; but like brute beasts, for the sake of a little pleasure of this corruptible life, they incur death of the soul.

entries.originalText: Thou therefore, my son, go not after thy lusts, but refrain thyself from thine appetites.(1) Delight thou in the Lord, and He shall give thee thy heart’s desire.(2)
entries.modernizedText: You therefore, My son, do not go after your lusts, but restrain yourself from your appetites.(1) Delight in the Lord, and He will give you your heart’s desire.(2)

entries.originalText: “For if thou wilt truly find delight, and be abundantly comforted of Me, behold in the contempt of all worldly things and in the avoidance of all worthless pleasures shall be thy blessing, and fulness of consolation shall be given thee.
entries.modernizedText: “For if you would truly find delight and be abundantly comforted by Me, behold, in the contempt of all worldly things and in the avoidance of all worthless pleasures will be your blessing, and fullness of consolation will be given you.

entries.originalText: And the more thou withdrawest thyself from all solace of creatures, the more sweet and powerful consolations shalt thou find.
entries.modernizedText: And the more you withdraw yourself from all solace of creatures, the more sweet and powerful consolations you will find.

entries.originalText: But at the first thou shalt not attain to them, without some sorrow and hard striving.
entries.modernizedText: But at first you will not attain them without some sorrow and hard striving.

entries.originalText: Long-accustomed habit will oppose, but it shall be overcome by better habit.
entries.modernizedText: Long-accustomed habit will oppose you, but it will be overcome by better habit.

entries.originalText: The flesh will murmur again and again, but will be restrained by fervour of spirit.
entries.modernizedText: The flesh will murmur again and again, but will be restrained by fervor of spirit.

entries.originalText: The old serpent will urge and embitter thee, but will be put to flight by prayer; moreover, by useful labour his entrance will be greatly obstructed.”
entries.modernizedText: The old serpent will urge and embitter you, but will be put to flight by prayer; moreover, by useful labor his entrance will be greatly obstructed.”
